mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances triggered by a >0.5% FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances triggered by a >0.5% UNRATE increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances triggered by a sustained RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react positively to increased economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances triggered by a >2% INDPRO increase.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure amidst tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances triggered by the specified conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in a month and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances triggered by the specified conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as broader economic activity is expected to improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following a sustained HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative, it signals a supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic slowdown concerns mount.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances triggered by the specified conditions.
